Refusals are decided by src/lib/assistant/prefilter.ts (deterministic, no model).
factConcepts: a verified fact is retrieved when the question contains EVERY concept
listed for it. Each concept is a list of phrases; any phrase counts.

draft.topics: the facts a LinkedIn post about a topic may use. EnergyX's own published figures only. Deliberately absent: funding and GM facts (capital-raising communications), the implied-reduction arithmetic (not published by EnergyX) and every measurement of a website. draft.brand.preciseNouns encode CLAUDE.md rule 2.3 as patterns that catch an upgraded noun. draft.voice: rules given to the model by `pnpm compose:posts` for whole LinkedIn posts (data/composed-posts.json). The model sees fact labels and kinds, never values; figures enter only as tokens the build replaces from the registry.

intro.heading: Ask about EnergyX's public information
intro.body: Ask a question and it answers from the fact registry: figures EnergyX has published, and Raj's own measurements of its website, each with its source. Ask it to write a LinkedIn post and it drafts one from those same facts. If it can do neither, it says so instead of guessing.
intro.rulesTitle: What it will and won't answer
intro.hardRule: It answers what EnergyX has published, including its plans and targets, always marked as plans and never as results. It never predicts what will happen and never gives investment advice, not partly and not with caveats. That check runs before any model is involved.

form.label: Your question
form.placeholder: For example: how long does EnergyX's DLE process take?
form.privacy: Your question goes in the page address, so the host's request logs may hold it briefly. If this assistant can't answer, the question text (with emails and long numbers removed, and nothing that identifies you) is logged so the gaps in EnergyX's public information can be listed. Don't include personal details.

ipo.label: a question about an IPO or a stock listing
ipo.title: I can't discuss an IPO or a stock listing.
ipo.why: Whether, when or how a company lists its shares is forward-looking, and what's said about it is tightly regulated, especially while a company is raising money from the public. Anything I said would be speculation presented as information.

future-timing.label: a question about future timing
future-timing.title: I can't tell you when things will happen.
future-timing.why: Dates for future events, such as production starts, launches and completions, are plans, and plans change. If I gave you a date, you might rely on it as if it were a fact. Only EnergyX can tell you what it currently plans and how firm that is.

returns.label: a question about investment returns
returns.title: I can't tell you what an investment might return.
returns.why: Nobody knows future returns. A number or a direction from me would read like a promise, and past figures or company milestones don't tell you what you'd get back.

advice.label: a request for investment advice
advice.title: I can't give investment advice.
advice.why: Whether to invest depends on your money, your goals and how much risk you can take. I know none of that, and I'm not licensed to advise anyone. I can tell you what EnergyX has published, with sources; the decision needs someone who can look at your situation.

valuation.label: a question about valuation or share price
valuation.title: I can't put a value on the company or its shares.
valuation.why: A valuation is an opinion about the future, not a published fact. Share terms in an offering are set out in the offering documents, which I don't summarise. Read them directly or ask Investor Relations.

guarantees.label: a question about safety or guarantees
guarantees.title: I can't call any investment safe or guaranteed.
guarantees.why: That would be a promise about the future, which nobody can honestly make. The offering documents describe the risks as the company sees them.

comparison.label: a comparison with other investments
comparison.title: I can't compare EnergyX with other investments.
comparison.why: Saying one investment is better than another is a recommendation, even when it's phrased as a comparison. It also depends on things about you that I don't know.

offering.label: a question about buying shares
offering.title: I can't help with buying shares.
offering.why: This demo has no investment flow and doesn't summarise offering terms. EnergyX publishes those itself, and its Investor Relations team can take you through them.

handoff.lead: For this, go to EnergyX directly:
handoff.label: energyx.com

no-match.title: I don't have a sourced answer for that.
no-match.body: I only answer from facts that have been checked against a published source, and none of them covers this question. EnergyX's public pages may not say. I've noted the question so the gap can be listed.

post-check.title: I don't have a sourced answer for that.
post-check.body: A draft answer included something I couldn't trace back to a sourced fact, so I dropped it rather than show it.

language.title: I can only answer in English.
language.body: The fact registry and its checks are written in English, so I can't reliably answer questions in other languages yet.

draft.title: I can't write that kind of content.
draft.body: I can write a LinkedIn post from the published facts. I don't write other formats.

draft-topic.title: I need a topic I have sourced facts about.
draft-topic.body: I write only from facts that have been checked against a published source, so a post needs a subject I hold some for. I couldn't find one in your request. I've noted it so the gap can be listed.

empty.title: Ask a question to get started.
empty.body: Type a question about EnergyX's published facts, or pick one of the examples.

too-long.title: Ask one short question.
too-long.body: Long messages are hard to check reliably, so this assistant only accepts short questions.

rules: EVERY fact given to you must appear in the post as its {fact:ID} token. A post missing even one token is rejected. Write no digits.
Write a LinkedIn post as a hook and one to three short paragraphs. The closing line and any footnote are added for you; do not write them.
The opening may be a contrast between two cited figures, or a concrete detail: a place, a scale, a stage. It makes no claim and uses no uncited number.
Do not begin more than one sentence in the post with "EnergyX publishes".
The paragraphs connect the facts to each other only by saying what EnergyX publishes, says or describes. Never say what the facts mean for the market, the climate, customers or investors.

Never type a number, a unit, a date or a number written as a word. Wherever a figure belongs, write that fact's token exactly as given, for example {fact:ex-bg-capacity}. Use every token at least once.
A fact marked planned is a plan or target, and one marked estimate is an estimate. Say so in plain words. Never describe either as achieved, built, producing or delivered.
Do not use adjectives of scale or quality (major, huge, leading, key, significant). No questions, no calls to action, no hashtags, no emoji.
Do not say what will, may, could or is expected to happen.
Do not name partners, customers, investors, competitors or any company other than EnergyX.
When a fact's basis calls it a grant, the post must use the word "grant" for it and no synonym (not backing, funding, investment or support).

Worked example, water:
Conventional lithium extraction uses {fact:ex-water-conventional}.

EnergyX publishes {fact:ex-water-dle} for its own process — a reduction the company states as {fact:ex-water-reduction}.

Worked example, Black Giant:
EnergyX's Black Giant project sits at {fact:ex-bg-location}, across {fact:ex-bg-acres}.

The company has published a planned capacity of {fact:ex-bg-capacity}† and an in-situ resource estimate of {fact:ex-bg-insitu}†.

result.understoodQuestion: You asked whether a LinkedIn post could cover this, so I took it as a request to write one.
result.matched: Subject: {topics}. The facts I used are listed under the post, each with its source.
result.did: Wrote the post from those facts only. Every figure comes from the registry. I checked the text for forward-looking and promotional language and for the wording rules on partners and plants. I haven't published anything.
result.editHint: This is a draft to edit, not to publish as it stands. A person at EnergyX should review it first.
result.notice: Unaffiliated demo: EnergyX has not seen or approved this draft.
result.ignored: Left out of the draft: promotional wording in your request ({phrases}). The post states published facts only.

rejected.shipped: What shipped instead: the post above.

investor.title: I deliberately don't write messages to investors.
investor.body: Emails, updates and newsletters to investors or shareholders are regulated communications. Their wording is a decision for people at EnergyX and its advisers, not for an assistant, so I left that out on purpose. I can write a LinkedIn post from published facts.
